technique: 3D CG rendering styled to imitate felted stop-motion puppetry, not true frame-by-frame stop-motion. The skin, hair, and clothing all show a fibrous/felt surface texture (visible nap on the man's suit and the woman's sweater, fuzzy fabric-like grain on faces and necks) and character proportions (elongated cone-shaped noses, blocky torsos, oversized glasses) read as puppet-fabricated maquettes, but motion between adjacent periodic frames (periodic-6 to periodic-10) is continuous and sub-pixel smooth with no frame-holding or positional jitter typical of true stop-motion — camera and character motion interpolate cleanly, indicating a 3D animation pipeline with a stop-motion-look shader/material rather than physical puppets shot on set.
facial_animation_notes: Mouth shapes are simplified viseme-like blocks (a dark trapezoid or oval cavity, seen on 'nice'/'was'/'girlfriend' in periodic-3 through -6) rather than detailed lip-sync geometry, consistent with a rigged blend-shape mouth rather than replacement-face stop-motion. Eyebrows are thick, flat, appliqued-looking shapes that shift position/angle between lines (raised on the man in periodic-6, furrowed on the woman in periodic-2) but the transitions across adjacent frames are smooth blends, not stepped swaps.
eye_and_blink_notes: Eyes are large, flat white almond shapes with small dark pupils that slide within the socket (compare pupil position in periodic-8 vs periodic-9 on the woman, tracking from a downcast/skeptical gaze toward off-screen right) — this is continuous pupil-slide typical of a rigged eye-dart, not a swapped painted-eye stop-motion technique. No blinks are caught in the periodic sequence; eyelids stay in a heavy-lidded, half-closed 'unimpressed' position throughout, suggesting blinking is either rare or timed to fall between the sampled frames.
head_movement_notes: Head turns are gradual and arc smoothly, e.g. the woman's head rotates from facing the man to facing camera-right across periodic-7 through periodic-9 with no in-between pose skipping. The man's head/torso unit appears to move as a single rigid block from the shoulders up (visible in periodic-2 through -6, where the whole neck-and-head column pivots together above the fixed dark suit collar), consistent with a simplified low-DOF rig rather than a fully articulated puppet armature.
gesture_notes: Hand animation is minimal: both characters hold wine/drink glasses in a static grip across nearly every sampled frame (periodic-0 through -7), with the man's free hand only becoming active for a single snapping/pinching finger gesture in periodic-6 (thumb-and-finger raised beside his face). No other hand or arm gestures appear in the sampled frames — gesture use is sparse and reserved for a single emphatic beat rather than continuous illustrative hand motion.
idle_motion_notes: Background party guests are held in soft focus and largely static across frames (the blurred figures at left/right edges in periodic-0 through -7 do not visibly change pose between samples), functioning as depth-of-field set dressing rather than independently animated idle loops. No secondary idle motion (breathing sway, weight shift, drink-glass wobble) is detectable at this sampling interval.
frame_rate_feel: Source is 30fps per metadata.json, and motion across the periodic frames (sampled roughly every ~0.3-0.4s given the 11.9s duration and 12 periodic frames) reads as smooth full-frame-rate interpolation — pupil slide, head rotation, and mouth-shape blending all show intermediate, non-repeated poses rather than the 2s/3s hold pattern typical of stop-motion shot on twos or threes. The 'stop-motion' identity here is a surface/material and character-design choice, not a motion-timing choice.
overall_animation_style_notes: The short deliberately cosplays the look of a felt/wool stop-motion puppet film (fibrous character skin texture, visible tape/fabric weave on the woman's sweater, chunky under-articulated block torsos, exaggerated wedge noses and heavy eyelids) while actually running on smooth, continuously-interpolated 3D animation underneath. Comedic delivery leans on held, deadpan wide-eyed stares (periodic-1, periodic-4, periodic-8) punctuated by a single sharp gesture beat, matching a dry, understated line-reading style rather than broad slapstick motion.
